name: Spite-Arid
geological_features: Glass desert formed by ancient asteroid impact
Razor-sharp obsidian ridges protruding from sand
Extreme temperature differentials cracking surface rock in real time
specific_features: Sand composition includes microscopic metallic fragments that destroy equipment seals
description: Spite-Arid is a small desert world whose surface seems specifically engineered to destroy anything that touches it. A glass desert formed by an ancient asteroid impact covers the equatorial region, its surface fractured into shards that slice through standard boot material. Obsidian ridges protrude from the sand at unpredictable angles, and the extreme temperature differentials between day and night cause surface rock to crack with audible reports.

The thin atmosphere provides no cushion against the temperature swings, which can exceed one hundred and seventy degrees within a single rotation. The sand itself is laced with microscopic metallic fragments that work their way into equipment seals and joints, grinding them to failure with a persistence that feels malicious.

No life has gained a foothold on Spite-Arid, and geological analysis suggests no life has ever existed here. The planet formed in conditions hostile to organic chemistry and has maintained that hostility with unwavering consistency for billions of years, a world that never offered anything and never will.

The silicon deposits are pure but the extraction costs are prohibitive given the equipment attrition rate. Spite-Arid's primary contribution to the sector is as a training ground for extreme-environment engineering students, who spend a standard week on the surface learning, through direct experience, that some worlds simply refuse to cooperate.
